topics.title: Introduction to agriculture
topics.unit: G11 Unit 1 – Introduction to Agriculture; G12 1.1.3, 4.1.3
topics.concept: Agriculture is an industry that supplies food, income, raw materials, employment and foreign currency. Eritrea has nomadic, semi-nomadic and sedentary agro-pastoral farming systems.

subtopics.title: Roles of agriculture and livestock; agro-industries
subtopics.concept: Agriculture is treated as an industry (G12 4.1.3). It supplies raw materials to food-processing, textile, leather, brewery and sugar industries (G11 1.2.4). Livestock plough land, provide manure, food, income and employment (G12 1.1.3).

subtopics.title: Farming systems in Eritrea
subtopics.concept: Sedentary agro-pastoralism (mixed farming) ≈ 67 % of farmers – dominant. Nomadic pastoralism prevails in the semi-desert zone. Semi-nomadic pastoralism (transhumance) occurs in spate-irrigation areas such as Sheeb.

subtopics.title: Branches of agricultural science
subtopics.concept: Plant sciences: agronomy, horticulture, plant breeding and protection. Animal sciences: nutrition, breeding, aquaculture, etc. Veterinary science is listed under production support and management.

subtopics.title: Constraints on agricultural development
subtopics.concept: Yield-defining factors (CO₂, solar radiation, temperature, humidity, crop physiology, altitude, latitude, crop/breed type) cannot be changed much; yield-limiting factors (water, N, P, K) can be supplied; yield-reducing factors are weeds, pests and diseases.

topics.title: Natural resource base
topics.concept: Climate, soil, biodiversity, water and agro-ecological zones form the resource base of agriculture.

subtopics.title: Climate elements and weather instruments
subtopics.concept: Isotherms join places of equal mean temperature. Instruments: rain gauge (rainfall), barometer/barograph (pressure), sunshine recorder (sunshine hours/intensity), radiometer (radiation), thermo-hygrograph (temperature and humidity), anemometer (wind).

subtopics.title: Soil roles, formation and profile
subtopics.concept: Five roles of soil: plant growth, habitat for organisms, nutrient recycling, water supply and purification, engineering medium. Soil-forming factors: parent material, climate, biota, topography and time. Profile: O (litter), A (humus-rich topsoil), B (subsoil, illuviation), C (weathered parent material), R (bedrock).

textbook_refs.section: 2.2 Soil (five major ecological roles of soil, Figure 2.2)

subtopics.title: Physical and chemical soil properties
subtopics.concept: Bulk density = dry mass/total volume; particle density = dry mass/volume of solids; porosity = pore volume/total volume; water content = (W1 − W2)/W1 × 100. Physical properties: texture, structure, consistency. Chemical: pH, colloids, ion exchange, salinity; lime supplies Ca (and Mg from dolomite).

textbook_refs.section: 2.2.11 Chemical Properties of Soil – calcareous and dolomitic soils
2.2.3 Soil Composition – bulk density, particle density, porosity
2.2.7 Measurement Techniques for Soil Water – gravimetric method

subtopics.title: Biodiversity conservation in Eritrea
subtopics.concept: Ten themes include integrated management, sustainable use, management of alien invasive species, in-situ and ex-situ conservation.

textbook_refs.section: 2.3.3 Causes of Wildlife Decline – alien species

subtopics.title: River basins of Eritrea
subtopics.concept: Setit (rises in central Ethiopia), Mereb-Gash (upper basin badly eroded), Barka-Anseba, Red Sea (flows used for spate irrigation and aquifer recharge) and Danakil (short runoff events).

textbook_refs.section: 2.4.3 The Major River Basins of Eritrea

subtopics.title: Agro-ecological zones
subtopics.concept: Six zones: moist highland, arid highland, moist lowland, arid lowland, sub-humid (700–1100 mm, 1 % of area) and semi-desert (< 200 mm, 39 % of area – largest and driest).

topics.title: Crop production and horticulture
topics.concept: Principles of plant growth, field crops, cultural practices, cropping systems and horticulture (nurseries and propagation).

subtopics.title: Plant structure, nutrients and photoperiod
subtopics.concept: Dicots: two cotyledons, flower parts in 4s or 5s, reticulate veins, tap root (beans, tomato, pumpkin); monocots: maize, sorghum, barley. Micronutrients: Mn, Fe, Mo, Cu, B, Zn, Cl. Long-day plants need > 12 h light (e.g. wheat); short-day < 12 h.

textbook_refs.section: 3.1.7 Climatic Factors – b) Classification based on day length

subtopics.title: Classification of field crops
subtopics.concept: Forage crops are grown for feed (hay, silage, pasture). Catch (emergence) crops are quick-growing annuals sown after a crop failure. Cover, green-manure and companion crops have other purposes.

subtopics.title: Land preparation, seed, weeds, pests and cultivation
subtopics.concept: Germination % = germinated/total × 100. Weeds compete with crops but also give feed, manure, medicine and building material. Resistant varieties are the cheapest and best insect control. Cultivation controls weeds, aerates soil and conserves moisture.

textbook_refs.section: 3.3.6 Weeds, Insects and Diseases – insect control

subtopics.title: Cropping systems
subtopics.concept: Mono-cropping, mixed cropping, intercropping, alley cropping, fallowing and crop rotation (different crops in sequence on the same land).

subtopics.title: Horticulture, nurseries and propagation
subtopics.concept: Pomology – fruits; olericulture – vegetables; floriculture – flowers. Nurseries raise seedlings (peasant, standard, temporary). Seeds are easy to store, handle and sow by machine; vegetative propagation gives true-to-type plants.

topics.title: Livestock production
topics.concept: Classification, feeds, breeds, routine management, housing and health of farm animals.

subtopics.title: Classification, digestive systems and terminology
subtopics.concept: Perissodactyla (odd-toed): horses, donkeys. Even-toed: cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, camels. Poultry digestive tract: crop, proventriculus, gizzard, intestines, caeca, cloaca (no rumen). Goat: buck, doe, kid, wether.

textbook_refs.section: 1.1.4 Types and Classification of Livestock – digestive systems

subtopics.title: Feeds and feeding systems
subtopics.concept: Dry matter = feed − water. Concentrates (grains, brans, cakes) are high-energy, low-fibre; roughages (hay, straw, stover) are fibrous. Lipids give 2.25 × the energy of carbohydrates. Zero grazing = cut-and-carry.

textbook_refs.section: 1.2.2 Common Classifications and Types of Feeds
1.2.2 Common Classifications and Types of Feeds
1.2.1 Feeds and Feed Composition – water and dry matter
1.2.2 Common Classifications and Types of Feeds – grazing management

subtopics.title: Breeds and breeding
subtopics.concept: Beef breeds: Angus, Hereford, Simmental, Charolais, Limousin, Gelbvieh, Brahman, Shorthorn. Dairy: Holstein-Friesian, Jersey, Guernsey, Brown Swiss, Ayrshire. Genetic improvement by selection, cross-breeding and artificial insemination; feeding, housing and disease control improve the environment.

textbook_refs.section: 1.3 Routine Management Practices – dairy breeds and milk fat

subtopics.title: Routine management practices
subtopics.concept: Culling, dehorning, castration, docking, shearing, hoof trimming and identification (tattooing, tagging, ear-notching, branding).

textbook_refs.section: 1.3 Routine Management Practices – j) Methods used to identify livestock

subtopics.title: Animal housing and equipment
subtopics.concept: Good houses: warm, well drained, ventilated, easy to clean, non-slippery floor. Dairy: tail-to-tail (easy milking, cleaning, supervision, less disease) vs head-to-head (easy feeding, narrow barns). Gags keep the jaws apart for oral dosing.

textbook_refs.section: 1.4 Animal Housing and Equipment – e) Dairy housing

subtopics.title: Diseases and parasites
subtopics.concept: TB is spread by raw milk and undercooked meat; controlled by hygiene, avoiding overcrowding, test-and-isolate. Ectoparasites (ticks, fleas, lice, flies, mites) live on the skin; endoparasites (roundworms, tapeworms, flukes) inside.

topics.title: Forestry and wildlife
topics.concept: Forest roles, deforestation, seedlings, enclosures, wildlife, laws, protected areas and challenges.

subtopics.title: Roles of forests
subtopics.concept: Tangible uses include wood products (timber, poles, firewood, charcoal) and non-wood products (gums, resins, incense, fruits, honey, medicine).

textbook_refs.section: 2.2.3 The Role of Forests – b) Tangible uses

subtopics.title: Deforestation and seedling planting
subtopics.concept: Anthropogenic causes: farm expansion, wood extraction, overgrazing, non-wood over-extraction, war. Bare-root seedlings are cheap, light and simple to raise but their roots dry out; potted seedlings survive better on difficult sites.

textbook_refs.section: 2.2.6 Seedling Planting – a) containerized and b) bare-root seedlings

subtopics.title: Enclosures/closures
subtopics.concept: Protected areas (usually steep, degraded slopes) where grazing and cutting are restricted so vegetation regenerates; they reduce erosion and siltation, conserve flora and fauna and reserve pasture.

subtopics.title: Wildlife roles, decline, conflict and challenges
subtopics.concept: Roles: food, science, aesthetics/heritage, tourism. Causes of decline: habitat destruction, drought, illegal trade, hunting, war, alien species, cultural beliefs. Conflict analysed with DPSIR. Challenges: poverty, beliefs, ownership and responsibility.

subtopics.title: Laws and protected areas
subtopics.concept: Proclamation 155/2006: forestry and wildlife; Proclamation 156/2006: plant quarantine. Protected areas: Gash-Setit (elephants), Semenawi Bahri (forest), Buri Peninsula (wild ass), Yob and Nakfa (Nubian ibex).

topics.title: Soil and water conservation
topics.unit: G12 Unit 3 – Soil and Water Conservation
topics.concept: Land degradation and erosion, conservation measures, surveying, water harvesting, irrigation and drainage.

subtopics.title: Land degradation and soil problems
subtopics.concept: Physical (structure deterioration), chemical (nutrient loss, salinity) and biological degradation. Speed and extent depend on soil type, relief, climate and intensity of land use. Major soil problems: acidity, salinity, alkalinity, compaction, erosion, swelling/shrinking clays.

textbook_refs.section: 3.1.2 The Importance of Soil and Water Conservation
3.1 Introduction – summary of soil degradation factors

subtopics.title: Soil erosion
subtopics.concept: Water erosion: splash (raindrop), sheet, rill, gully. Wind erosion: deflation, abrasion. Ice erosion: glacial, freeze–thaw.

textbook_refs.section: 3.2.3 Soil Erosion – water, ice and wind erosion

subtopics.title: Conservation measures and surveying
subtopics.concept: Physical: terraces, stone bunds, diversion ditches, waterways, gully control. Biological/agronomic: afforestation, enclosures, grass strips, crop rotation, intercropping, tillage. Slope % = VI/HI × 100.

subtopics.title: Water harvesting and irrigation
subtopics.concept: Dams store water for people, animals, irrigation and hydropower. Drip irrigation is the most water-efficient; sprinklers ≈ 75 %; furrow/basin 40–50 %.

subtopics.title: Drainage
subtopics.concept: Poor drainage: heavy rain, clay soils, sand over impermeable clay, hardpans. Advantages of drainage: aeration, deeper root zone, warmer soil and better nutrient uptake, more micro-organism activity, salinity control.

topics.title: Farm management
topics.concept: Farm management, factors of production, production economics, records and co-operatives.

subtopics.title: Importance of farm management
subtopics.concept: The manager plans and coordinates activities, buys inputs, keeps records and pays wages.

subtopics.title: Factors of production and economic principles
subtopics.concept: Factors: land, labour, capital, management, entrepreneurship. APP = TPP/X; MPP = ΔTPP/ΔX; MVP = MPP × output price; profit-maximizing input level where MVP = input price. Fixed costs (insurance, depreciation, housing) vs variable costs (fuel, repairs). Rainfall is uncontrollable.

textbook_refs.section: 4.1.5 Basic Economic Principles – controllable and uncontrollable factors
4.1.5 Basic Economic Principles – production function, AP, MP, MVP (Table 4.3)

subtopics.title: Farm records and financial statements
subtopics.concept: Petty cash book (only cash transactions), wage book, inventory. Depreciation = (CP − SV)/E; book value = CP − accumulated depreciation. Balance sheet = financial position on a date; income statement = period.

subtopics.title: Community-based organizations and co-operatives
subtopics.concept: Co-operatives have an economic purpose, are member-owned and controlled, run for members, not charities or state-directed. Principles: voluntary and open membership, democratic control, economic participation, autonomy, education, cooperation, concern for community.

textbook_refs.section: 4.4.2 Types of CBO – c) Co-operative principles
